Sorry for the particularly underwhelming title but, well... it is.

Without spoilers the best thesis I can give is it is a movie about the creation of artificial intelligence. And really the biggest things I love about it, is it manages to stay logical and intellectual, while remaining ambiguous and philosophical in its message and delivery. A lot of the movie is about humanitary ironies, about what is and isn't human, or just how blurred that spectrum of what quantifies something to be human. What is intelligence, what is human intelligence, and what isn't human intelligence. What are the ethical considerations and consequences of making a consciousness? What are the possible struggles that a new or non human consciousness can possess? If any of this has intrigued you, watch the film. You can easily find it online (torrents are still vastly available) and I believe it is on netflix. And I would suggest you do so. It has some of the best characterization for a situation like this I have ever seen, and really delves head first into concepts that I love to see taken seriously with regards to its setting and characters. While it does still do a thing I don't like with regards to some characters feeling a bit more evil than others, and some feelings that paint characters and their actions in a more cliche or stereotypical light than intended, I still enjoyed the movie wholly.

Existentialism is a concept I really enjoy, and to see it handled here so carefully and so well makes it something I recommend to anyone who enjoys science fiction. It is meticulate, artistic, intelligent, and ambiguous. To say anything out right here would be robbing the viewer an experience. It is what I like to see when it comes to the handling of characters in a work. There is not a right side, and arguably no good characters. And I appreciate that.
